subject: FintechCo deployment — follow-up & next steps (SSO / KMS / logging)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@fintechco.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo deployment — follow-up & next steps (SSO / KMS / logging)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet the team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on requirements that will drive deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private):

Summary of constraints from today:
- SSO: FintechCo requires SAML SSO (Okta) with SCIM provisioning and group mapping.
- KMS/HSM: You indicated a requirement for customer-managed keys (CMEK) and the ability to use an HSM-backed key (CloudHSM) for key material.
- Logging & retention: Audit logs + model invocation logs need 7 years retention and must be accessible for audits.
- Network: Preference for VPC/VPN connectivity; potential on-prem requirement for regulated workloads.

Attachments: FintechCo_Security_Questionnaire.pdf, SSO_diagram.png (SSO flow we sketched).

Our quick read: Hosted API will be easiest to get started but likely can’t meet KMS/HSM or VPC/on-prem needs. Dedicated capacity supports customer-managed KMS and configurable log shipping (we’ll confirm retention paths), while Private (VPC/on-prem) is the most straight-forward way to fully meet HSM and long-term retention/audit controls.

Proposed next steps:
1) Rafael — can you confirm the exact capabilities for CMEK/HSM integration and the recommended logging retention architecture?
2) Priya / Alex — please confirm if Dedicated would be acceptable if we can demonstrate CMEK with HSM-backed keys and a guaranteed 7-year audit log export to your S3/archive. If not, we’ll map Private deployment steps and timeline.
3) I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to go over the tradeoffs and the SOC2 artifacts you asked about.

Suggested times: Tue 8/3 9:30am PT or Wed 8/4 11:00am PT — let me know what works.

Thanks,

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachments: FintechCo_Security_Questionnaire.pdf, SSO_diagram.png

From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Jones <alex.jones@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FintechCo deployment — follow-up & next steps (SSO / KMS / logging)

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifications from the security team side so we can make a decision:

1) SSO: Okta SAML + SCIM are required. Group mapping and role sync are mandatory for least privilege.
2) KMS/HSM: We need CMEK and must be able to attest that the private key material is HSM-backed (we currently use AWS CloudHSM). If Dedicated can accept customer-controlled keys that are provably HSM-backed, that may be acceptable. If not, Private (VPC/on-prem) will likely be required.
3) Logs/retention: Audit trails and model invocation logs must be retained for 7 years. For compliance purposes we need immutable export (write-once) or a tamper-evident storage solution — putting logs to our S3 with object-lock would be ideal.
4) SOC2 / evidence: Please include SOC2 Type II report (if available) and any pen-test summaries or third-party risk assessments.
5) Network: We prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink for Dedicated; for on-prem we may need a VPN/Direct Connect plan.

Can Rafael confirm whether Dedicated supports: (a) CMEK + HSM-backed keys (with attestation), and (b) direct log export to customer-owned S3 with lifecycle/retention controls? Also timeline implications for Private deployment if that’s required.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Singh
Head of Security, FintechCo
priya.singh@fintechco.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@fintechco.com>, Alex Jones <alex.jones@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FintechCo deployment — follow-up & next steps (SSO / KMS / logging)

Hi Priya / Alex — thanks for the detailed list. Short answers up front, details below.

Summary:
- Hosted API: cannot meet CMEK/HSM or VPC peering requirements. Not recommended for regulated workloads.
- Dedicated: supports customer-managed keys and log export patterns; HSM-backed attestation depends on where key material is hosted.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full control — supports CloudHSM and local HSMs; easiest path for strict compliance.

Details:
1) CMEK / HSM:
- Dedicated: We support CMEK where customers bring keys via supported KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). For HSM-backed keys, if you host keys in AWS CloudHSM we can integrate via customer KMS + external key material workflow. We can produce an attestation that keys are customer-controlled, but a cryptographic proof of HSM residency depends on your KMS setup. We’ll document the exact flows in a short tech note.
- Private: Full support — customer keys can live in your CloudHSM or on-prem HSM and Redwood runs in your VPC/on-prem.

2) Logging & retention:
- Dedicated: We can stream logs and model invocation events to a customer-owned S3 bucket (or an external SIEM) using secure, signed write connectors. From there you control lifecycle policies and immutability (S3 Object Lock / Vault). This is the recommended path to guarantee 7-year retention without Redwood holding long-term copies.
- Private: Native retention within your environment; you control storage and immutability.

3) Network:
- Dedicated supports VPC peering, PrivateLink, and dedicated egress IPs. For on-prem we support VPN/Direct Connect options.

4) SOC2 / artifacts:
- I’ll attach the Redwood SOC2 Type II summary and our pen-test exec summary. Full SOC2 and supplementary docs can be shared under an NDA / secure link.

I’m attaching a short architecture note (redwood-dedicated-architecture.pdf) that maps each requirement to the recommended deployment mode and a SSO/KMS/Logging checklist. I’ll follow up with the exact steps for integrating CloudHSM + AWS KMS in the Dedicated model and an estimated timeline for a Private deployment (including packaging and on-prem install windows).

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll produce a 2-page mapping doc by Mon 8/2.
- If Dedicated looks viable after that, we can scope an initial pilot (isolated pool) and run an integration PoC for SSO + KMS + log export. If not, we’ll kick off Private deployment planning.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood-dedicated-architecture.pdf
